comparator.name: Culture and Education (Algemene Cultuurwetenschappen)
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized registry target is Algemene Cultuurwetenschappen (English display name Culture Studies), recognized programme code 56823. Tilburg currently presents this Dutch-language enrolment route as the Culture and Education bachelor track within Algemene Cultuurwetenschappen, while the same recognized programme family also contains the international Digital Culture and Society route. The official 2026–27 Culture and Education page reconstructs all 180 ECTS: a shared 60-ECTS first year, a 60-ECTS second year with a required Culture or Education specialisation, and a 60-ECTS third year. The neutral official-order rule selects Culture, the first specialisation listed, independently of UCR fit. Its 12-ECTS cultural-institution internship and 30-ECTS open minor or mobility window are retained explicitly rather than filled with invented fixed subjects. Zero-credit GROW development is excluded from the 180-ECTS component total.
components: Big Ideas: Changing Views on Nature
Art and Media in a Digital Society

routeSelection.basis: The programme requires students to choose Culture or Education after the shared first year, while the normalized target does not name a specialisation. Culture is selected because the official 2026–27 page lists it first, independently of UCR course availability.

alternatives.label: Culture, heritage & public education
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres art, literature, media, cultural history, heritage and museums while retaining communication, sociology, philosophy and research relevant to public-facing cultural education.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to the selected Culture specialisation combines cultural history, art and heritage, literature, film and media, identity and society, rhetoric, qualitative methods and independent humanities research.
progression: Foundations in art history, literature, media, history and sociology precede advanced museum, heritage, film, literary, communication and research work. All formal prerequisites and verified semester offerings are respected; eight level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Digital culture, media & AI society
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum concentrates on media, communication, data, platforms, AI, identity, politics and social research, matching the programme family’s international digital-culture direction.
alternatives.concept: A distinct digital-culture pathway connecting critical media analysis and communication to data science, computer vision, databases, machine learning, political ideas, social theory, cognition and AI-related research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, thirteen courses replace much of the art-history, heritage, broad literature and historical-research sequence with rhetoric, data science, computer vision, databases, machine learning, platform media, politics and cognition.
progression: Introductory communication, film/media, data science and brain-and-behaviour work precede advanced platforms, machine learning, representation, psycholinguistics and research. Formal prerequisites and verified semester offerings are respected; eight level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Language, learning & education in society
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines literature, rhetoric and communication with social, developmental and learning sciences, research methods, diversity and public questions.
alternatives.concept: A distinct education-oriented pathway combining language, literature and communication with learning, social psychology, developmental psychology, youth, diversity, sociology, ethics and quantitative and qualitative research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, eleven courses replace most art-history, museum, film and heritage depth with rhetoric, communication, social psychology, developmental psychology, youth, learning and quantitative research. It differs from the digital-culture pathway in fifteen courses and has a clearly educational rather than computational organising logic.
progression: Literature, rhetoric, brain-and-behaviour, social psychology, history, sociology and research-methods foundations precede advanced persuasion, literary meaning, social theory, youth and lifespan development, creative communication and public social questions. All formal prerequisites and verified semester offerings are respected; eight level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the target’s culture-specialisation, heritage, art/media, cultural change, diversity and Culture and Education interests. Two further coherent generator clusters pass evidence, feasibility and distinctness: the international Digital Culture and Society direction becomes UCR-2, and the formal Education specialisation becomes UCR-3. The three-alternative maximum is reached, and every generator-eligible interest row is owned exactly once.

notes.text: Tilburg’s selected Culture route includes a compulsory 12-ECTS placement in a museum, library, heritage organisation or related cultural institution, a 30-ECTS open minor or mobility window and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can assemble strong cultural, media, heritage, education and research curricula, but its scheduled catalogue does not reproduce the compulsory professional placement or a teacher-qualification route; the open minor is not filled with invented content.

The current Culture and Education track is bilingual in year 1 and Dutch-taught in years 2 and 3, whereas UCR is English-taught. This comparison assesses academic content and structure rather than language of instruction.
